solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Project completed for Chinese government

parts.note: a match or task that is over is completed
the Han are the majority ethnic group of China

explanation.surface: A building scheme finished on behalf of the authorities in Beijing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' reads as a noun, a scheme, but it is the verb meaning to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to jut out beyond the surface below, which is exactly what a ledge or roof edge does.

clue.text: Giuseppe burned, shedding skin

indicators.note: losing its skin means the outer letter at each end of the synonym is stripped away

parts.note: food that is burned has been overcooked, i.e. someone overdid it

explanation.surface: An Italian man called Giuseppe got sunburnt and is now peeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding skin' removes the first and last letters (O and D) from OVERDID.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer, so his first name identifies him.

clue.text: Dump run down old banger

parts.note: to run something down is to criticise it, or to rubbish it
a banger is British slang for a decrepit old car, also called a heap

explanation.surface: Someone disparages a decrepit car and wants it scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a battered old car (it also means a sausage).
explanation.definitionFit: A dump is a place where refuse is piled, a synonym for a tip or midden.

clue.text: The ratings are bound to go up after this broadcast

definitions.text: The ratings are bound to go up after this broadcast

parts.words: The ratings are bound to go up after this broadcast
parts.note: sounds like TV viewing figures rising, but ratings are naval sailors, who climb to the top deck when this order is called over the ship's tannoy

explanation.surface: A TV executive is confident a programme will boost the viewing figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratings are ordinary sailors in the Royal Navy, and 'go up' means climbing up from below decks.
explanation.definitionFit: The shipboard command summons every crew member up top, so the sailors must climb up after hearing it.

clue.text: Quarrel with sergeant about battle order

indicators.note: about indicates the letters of the two words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier argues with his sergeant over the arrangement of troops for combat.
explanation.definitionFit: This naval command orders all crew to their combat stations, so it is a call to battle readiness.

clue.text: Great tackle stifles goal attempt

indicators.note: the phrase smothers the letters within it, concealing the word inside

explanation.surface: A defender's fine challenge blocks a shot on goal.
explanation.definitionFit: In football an offensive move towards goal is a strike or assault on the opponents' defence.

clue.text: I toast sanction-busting call to arms

indicators.note: busting suggests the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A drinker raises a glass to breaking sanctions, a rallying cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the military order for troops to take their battle positions, a summons to fight.

clue.text: Take wickets of openers, getting a pair

indicators.note: openers, like batsmen opening an innings, are the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler takes the opening batsmen's wickets, getting two.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a couple, the number that comes after one.

clue.text: Faithfully recorded Callas performing outside broadcast on Radio Three

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged name goes around the other piece
performing suggests the singer's name is put to work in a new arrangement

parts.note: sic is written after a quotation to show it is copied exactly as in the original

explanation.surface: An opera singer's recital is relayed on the BBC's music station.
explanation.walkthrough: BBC Radio 3 is the UK's serious-music station and Maria Callas a celebrated soprano; 'performing' is the anagram signal and 'outside' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio 3 chiefly airs orchestral and operatic repertoire, so its output is of that genre.

clue.text: Representative of "The People's Bishop" involved in court case

indicators.note: involved in means one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: a court case is a trial
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A spokesman for a populist cleric is caught up in a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes what belongs to or typifies a people or clan, so it characterises a community.

clue.text: News at Ten interrupts a Liberal citizen

indicators.note: interrupts means the phrase breaks into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: N is short for new, so two of them make news
IO, looking like the digits 1 and 0, stands for ten

explanation.surface: The evening TV bulletin cuts into a Liberal politician's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is a British TV news bulletin. Here 'News' is split as N + N (new, plural).
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a person belonging to a particular country, a synonym for a citizen of it.

clue.text: Low-scoring draw between France and Japan briefly reported in The Nation

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
a low-scoring draw is a 1-1 result; each 1 is read as the letter I and goes after one team's initial
J is a short form of Japan, as in the JPN-style abbreviation shortened to its first letter
a low-scoring draw is a 1-1 result; each 1 is read as the letter I and goes after one team's initial

explanation.surface: A football paper reports a dull one-all game between France and Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'low-scoring draw' is 1-1, and its two 1s, read as the letter I, follow F and J in the reported scoreline F 1 J 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiji is an independent island country in the South Pacific.

clue.text: She answers a higher calling during turbulent times!

definitions.text: She answers a higher calling during turbulent times!

parts.words: She answers a higher calling during turbulent times!
parts.note: sounds like a nun in troubled days, but describes cabin crew responding to call buttons at altitude when the plane hits turbulence

explanation.surface: A devout woman follows her vocation in an era of upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'higher calling' suggests religion; it is a passenger's call button pressed at cruising height.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewardess on an airliner attends to passengers who summon her during a bumpy flight.

clue.text: For the doctor's travel magazine, a feature penned by Julius

parts.note: Time is a US news magazine

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed within the setter's word

parts.note: the setter Julius refers to himself, so this gives me
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A travel magazine runs an article the setter wrote, aimed at a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor is Doctor Who, the TV time traveller whose TARDIS takes him through history.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor's TARDIS is a device for journeying through the ages, which is how he travels.

clue.text: Lops head off plant

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A gardener beheads a plant with a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family flower, associated in Greek myth with the underworld.

clue.text: Randy (a bloke from Riga) picked up a bit of litter

indicators.note: picked up, as a microphone picks up speech, signals the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: randy means sexed up, and a man from Riga, the Latvian capital, is a Lett

explanation.surface: A lustful Latvian man bends to collect a scrap of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like rubbish but means a brood of young born together.
explanation.definitionFit: One of six offspring born at a single birth is one member of a litter.

clue.text: Blades come from this mighty club!

definitions.meaning: the spice is sold as blades, the dried lacy coating of the nutmeg seed
a heavy medieval spiked war club

explanation.surface: Swords are forged from some powerful cudgel, or a strong sports team produces players called the Blades.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the nutmeg-husk spice, sold in strips called blades, and a heavy battle club.

clue.text: See 6
Rose Cottage finally gets drive connection

parts.note: Axl Rose is the lead singer of Guns N' Roses

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cottage named Rose Cottage at last gets a driveway linked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod joining a vehicle's wheels transmits the drive from the engine, linking them.

clue.text: The Spanish mutiny about working early

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
working suggests the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A rebellion in Spain breaks out before its time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' could be the anagram signal, but 'working' does that job and 'about' wraps the result around the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untimely happens prematurely, before its proper time.

clue.text: See 4
Horrid giant rodent's first seen after spring. Horrid giant rodent!

indicators.note: seen after places the anagram behind the synonym for spring

parts.note: to spring is to jump

indicators.note: horrid suggests the letters are a mess and need setting right
first picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A huge, nasty rat appears in springtime; the clue ends with a shudder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrid' rearranges GIANT plus R as INGRAT. The definition repeats the clue's words: the whole second sentence names the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant jumping rat of Madagascar is a large rodent, so the phrase fits the creature.

clue.text: The last character to be chauffeured, like Julius in St. Petersburg?

indicators.note: to be, with chauffeured, means the letter goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: to be chauffeured is to be driven in a car
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A setter imagines being driven around Russia's old capital as the final passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: Julius suggests Julius Caesar, whose title gave Russia its word for an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian emperor's title derives from Caesar, so a Caesar in St Petersburg was a tsar.

clue.text: Say goodbye to Fatty; take some exercise!

indicators.note: take means subtract these letters from the other word

parts.note: adipose means fatty, as in adipose tissue
PE is physical education, i.e. exercise

explanation.surface: A dieter tells a plump person to work out, or bids a fat friend farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' removes P and E from ADIPOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for farewell, used in English as a casual way of bidding someone so long.

clue.text: Boycott, opener for England and Yorkshire, gutted to get injury

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as in a trade union ban

indicators.note: opener for takes the opening letter of the word
gutted removes the insides, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott, opening batsman for England and Yorkshire, is crushed by an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England and Yorkshire opening batsman, which disguises 'Boycott' as the verb to black (ban).
explanation.definitionFit: A shiner, bruising round the eye from a blow, is a common facial injury.

clue.text: McQueen regularly used a prompt

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the name

explanation.surface: Steve McQueen often relied on an off-screen prompt for his lines.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's cue is the signal telling them to speak or enter, a prompt.

clue.text: Am I to be sacked from paper, folding in the spring?

indicators.note: to be sacked from means these letters are dismissed from the other word

parts.note: origami is the Japanese art of paper folding
the letters of these words are taken away

explanation.surface: A newspaper employee wonders if they will be fired when the paper closes in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folding' looks like a paper going bust, but 'paper folding' together is origami.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a source, the place where a river begins, so it is a starting point.

clue.text: Sci-fi series rejected pitch featuring a dash of nudity

indicators.note: featuring means the other letter is included inside
rejected means the pitch synonym is thrown out of the title

parts.note: Star Trek is the science-fiction TV series
tar is black pitch

explanation.surface: A sci-fi show turns down a proposal containing a brief nude scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a sales proposal; it is tar.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to dash naked through a public place, so a streak is a brief naked run.

clue.text: Tense scenes! Dr. Seuss put in prison!

indicators.note: put in means the prison synonym is placed inside the rearranged name
Dr. stands for doctored, so the name is tampered with

parts.note: pen is short for penitentiary, a prison

explanation.surface: Dramatic moments as the children's author Dr Seuss is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr.' rearranges SEUSS as SUSSE, and PEN is 'put in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the tension of uncertainty, what audiences feel in nail-biting scenes.
